description: Command-query separation: each method either changes state or returns data, never both.
Command and query responsibility segregation: a write model with domain rules for commands and a separate read model of DTOs for queries, in one database or several.
Data shaped for a screen or API response, such as a LINQ projection or a denormalized table, with no business rules.
A class that executes one business intent, such as `PlaceOrder`, by loading or creating an aggregate, calling its methods and saving.
A class that implements the same interface as the handler it wraps, adding behavior such as logging or a transaction before and after the inner call.
An object that receives a request and routes it to its handler through a pipeline, which MediatR implements as `IMediator.Send`.
